title: FFNM HUMECTANT OPTIMIZATION
summary: Among the virile segment of smokers, simultaneously low levels of both propylene glycol and glycerin results in the optimization or near optimization of all of the significant attributes in this group. Specifically, this combination of humectants increases strength, tobacco taste, natural taste, fresh aftertaste and ease of getting smoke through the filter, while it decreases bitter taste, strong aftertaste and mildness. Furthermore, both measures of acceptance are relatively high in this region of humectants. Given the trade-offs associated with key attributes and acceptance measures, the optimal area of humectants among the franchise group of smokers of simultaneously low propylene glycol and glycerin, harshness, natural taste and tobacco taste are optimized in this area, while both acceptance measures are near optimization. Only dry aftertaste is adversely affected in this area of opportunity. The results of the action standard group of smokers were not as consistent as those of the virile or franchise groups of smokers. Each area of humectants among the action standard smokers illustrates unique strengths and weaknesses. Considering the trade-offs associated with each area of opportunity, the two most desirable regions are simultaneously low propylene glycol and glycerin and simultaneously moderate propylene glycol and glycerin. Simultaneously low propylene glycol and glycerin results in a moderately accepted product with relatively good performance on strength, draw, tobacco taste and bitter taste. However, this combination of humectants does tend to adversely affect sweet aftertaste.
